title: Fix fallback heuristic off-by-one causing tenant misroutes to lower-tier models/regions
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary: Several customers reported production misroutes where requests were routed to lower-tier models or to non-preferred regions after the primary capacity threshold was reached. Impact spanned Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments for tenants that rely on strict model and region affinity. Root cause analysis found a deterministic tie-break and comparator bug in the fallback selection code plus a policy serialization/versioning mismatch between control plane and node runtime.

Observed customer symptoms: increased latency, degraded output quality, higher per-token costs (unexpected model choices), and confusion when customers had pinned model versions but saw different variants. Support tickets escalated from three enterprise customers and multiple internal alerts for elevated error rates and latency tail.

Technical root causes (summary):
- Fallback comparator used an inclusive boundary (<=) which, combined with floating-point score normalization, allowed the next-tier candidate to be considered equal and selected incorrectly (off-by-one style error in priority buckets).
- The tie-breaker relied on iterating an unordered map (Go map) which produced non-deterministic ties across nodes, so different nodes made different fallback choices for the same policy and request characteristics.
- Control plane encoded fallback policies without an explicit version/hash. When we deployed a policy change, some runtimes pulled a partially-updated policy object and applied it, causing transient mismatched behavior during rollout.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Rolled back control-plane policy change that introduced the new packing order (2026-03-11 03:00 UTC).
- Applied temporary region-affinity override for the three most-impacted tenants to force selection to their pinned region/model while a fix is developed and rolled out. This was coordinated with SEs and documented in the three support tickets.
- Added short-term alert on divergence between control-plane policy hash and node-reported policy hash so we can auto-detect stale/partial applications.

Proposed permanent fix:
1) Correct comparator logic: change inclusive comparator to strict (<) for primary bucket selection and normalize floating comparisons with eps tolerance.
2) Deterministic ordering: replace unordered map iteration with an explicit priority-sorted list and an explicit tie-breaker: (a) policy-defined priority, (b) region affinity score, (c) stable node-assigned UUID if still tied.
3) Policy versioning: include an immutable policy version and SHA256 hash in the serialized policy. Runtime must verify hash and reject partial applications. Control plane will use a two-phase apply: PREPARE -> VALIDATE -> ACTIVATE.
4) Add unit tests for comparator edge cases, property-based tests for tie scenarios, and an integration test that simulates a mixed-simulated-node rollout. Add e2e test in the CI that exercises Hosted/Dedicated/Private permutations.
5) Canary plan: push to runtime-1.22 canary cluster (us-west-2 small pool) with feature flag `deterministic-fallback-v2`. Observe for 48h, then expand to dedicated pools, then to Private via opt-in upgrade.

Monitoring and SLOs to add:
- New metric: `routing.fallback.divergence_rate` (percent requests where control-plane hash != node hash).
- New alert: divergence_rate > 0.5% for 10m triggers automated rollback of recent policy activation.
- Dashboard: per-tenant misroute count, model-selection distribution, and latency/cost delta for impacted tenants.

Rollout and rollback plan:
- PR created and linked below. Target canary deploy 2026-03-16, monitor 48h, staged regional rollouts 2026-03-18 -> 2026-03-21. If divergence or elevated customer error rate appears, rollback to runtime-1.21 policy behavior using the control-plane versioning API.

Customer communication: SEs have drafts for the three escalations (links below) and we will send an interim update summarizing the rollback and the planned fix timeline. Final postmortem will be shared with customers and updated in the public incident log.

Postmortem action items (tentative):
- Create a runbook for policy apply failures and partial rollouts (owner: Reliability).
- Audit existing policy application codepaths for other implicit ordering or map iteration patterns (owner: Platform).
- Add tenancy-focused validation rules so tenants with pinned models/regions are opt-protected from fallback when they mark strict affinity.
